userStories.title: THREAD ASSIGN parsing
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Accept and validate THREAD ASSIGN payloads without weakening other job kinds.

**Motivation** — B1 places `THREAD` jobs only on runners that report protocol 4, and B3a built the session host's parts without wiring them. Until a runner can run a `THREAD` job end to end, no thread can start.

**Approach** — `parseAssign` accepts `command: 'THREAD'`. For a THREAD job: `profiles` must be `[]` (else `invalid profiles`), `bashMode` must be `'raw'` (else `invalid bashMode`), and `thread` must be an object (else `invalid thread`); a RUN, PLAN or config job carrying a `thread` key is `invalid thread`. The `thread` block, each field checked in this order:

| Field | Rule | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `threadId` | `assertSegment` | `invalid threadId` |
| `action` | `'SESSION'` (`PUBLISH` is phase C) | `invalid thread action` |
| `feature` | `assertFeature` | `invalid thread feature` |
| `resume` | boolean | `invalid thread resume` |
| `instructions` | string of at most 262144 characters | `invalid instructions` |
| `backend` | `{ kind: 'native', model?, effort? }` or `{ kind: 'acp', agent: 'claude' \| 'codex', model?, effort? }`; `model` matches `THREAD_MODEL_ID_RE`; `effort` matches `/^[a-z]{1,16}$/` | `invalid backend` |
| `skills` | array of objects whose `sourceId`, `owner`, `repo`, `sha` are strings and whose `skills` is an array of `{ name, dir, description }` strings | `invalid skills` |
| `initialMessage` | `null`, or `{ messageId, text }` with `messageId` passing `assertSegment` and `text` a string of at most `THREAD_LIMITS.messageMaxBytes` UTF-8 bytes | `invalid initialMessage` |

Only the listed fields are copied into `assign.thread` (an unknown key is dropped). The skill identifiers are validated again by `ensureSkills` before they reach a path.

**Scope** — In: parseAssign and field-focused unit specs. Out: session execution (US-003–005), CommandHandler routing (US-006), protocol bump (US-007), ACP session hosting (phase D; ACP payload validation remains in scope); `THREAD_PUBLISH`, `write_doc`, a `PUBLISH` action, a stale session start and Discard belong to phase C; the runner rejects `PUBLISH` at ASSIGN and `THREAD_PUBLISH` as `unsupported`.

**Interface** — `parseAssign(command: FleetCommandOut): ParsedAssign`; `ThreadAssign` and `THREAD_LIMITS` from `@nathapp/fleet-protocol`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: When `parseAssign` receives the valid THREAD fixture (`command: 'THREAD'`, job `feature: 'thread-t1'`, `profiles: []`, `bashMode: 'raw'`, `planFrom: null`, thread `threadId: 't1'`, `action: 'SESSION'`, thread `feature: 'brainstorm-x'`, `resume: false`, `instructions: 'be helpful'`, backend `{ kind: 'native', model: 'minimax/MiniMax-M3' }`, one skill source and `initialMessage: { messageId: 'm1', text: 'hi' }`), then `assign.thread` is deep-equal to the fixture's `thread` block.
AC-2: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture without `thread`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread' }`.
AC-3: When `parseAssign` receives a RUN ASSIGN carrying the fixture's `thread` block, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread' }`.
AC-4: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `profiles: ['fast']`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid profiles' }`.
AC-5: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `bashMode: 'gated'`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid bashMode' }`.
AC-6: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.threadId: '../t1'`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid threadId' }`.
AC-7: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.action: 'PUBLISH'`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread action' }`.
AC-8: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.feature: '../x'`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid thread feature' }`.
AC-9: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.backend: { kind: 'native', model: 'm/x[high]' }`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid backend' }`.
AC-10: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.backend: { kind: 'acp', agent: 'claude' }`, then it returns `ok: true`.
AC-11: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.skills: 'none'`, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid skills' }`.
AC-12: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.initialMessage.text` of 32769 ASCII characters, then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid initialMessage' }`.
AC-13: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.initialMessage: null`, then it returns an `assign.thread` whose `initialMessage` is `null`.
AC-14: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with an extra `thread.extra: 1`, then it returns an `assign.thread` that has no `extra` key.
AC-15: When `parseAssign` receives the fixture with `thread.initialMessage.text` of 11000 characters `'中'` (33000 UTF-8 bytes), then it returns `{ ok: false, detail: 'invalid initialMessage' }`.

routing.reasoning: Single parser branch and tests with existing validation helpers; no new concurrency or auth implementation.

userStories.title: Thread log stream and threadBackends report
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Ship the thread JSONL stream through LogShipper and advertise only credential-backed native models.

**Motivation** — B1 places `THREAD` jobs only on runners that report protocol 4, and B3a built the session host's parts without wiring them. Until a runner can run a `THREAD` job end to end, no thread can start.

**Approach** — `LogStreamName` becomes `LogEventPayload['stream'] | typeof THREAD_STREAM` (the legacy `log` event payload is not widened). `LogJob` becomes `NaxLogJob | ThreadLogJob`; the shipper narrows on it wherever it reads `spec.sources` (`register`, `lacksRun`, `discover`). `register` of a `ThreadLogJob` adds a single stream `thread` at `threadPath` (no `stdout`, no `stderr`, no run-log search); `wake`, `drain`, `stopJob` and the upload rules are unchanged. `ServerClient.putLog` already builds `/fleet/runner/jobs/<jobId>/logs/<stream>`.

`NaxCapabilityProbe.probe` asks `nax auth list --json` for the union of the profiles' providers and `nativeModelProviders(naxHome)`, sorted and without duplicates, then adds `threadBackends: { native: (await readNativeModels(naxHome, <providerIds whose credential is available>)).models, acp: [] }`. `StaticCapabilityProbe` reports no `threadBackends` (a runner.json capability override cannot host threads).

**Scope** — In: log type union, one-stream registration, native provider auth/probe, the existing ServerClient PUT URL for `thread`, and corresponding specs. Out: ThreadJobRun stream registration (US-003), first-sync daemon capability reporting (US-007). The API accepting, folding and pricing the `thread` stream, cost accounting from `usage` lines and the content SSE belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-ingest` (B2); until then the API refuses `PUT .../logs/thread` and `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` stays off.

**Interface** — `LogStreamName = LogEventPayload['stream'] | typeof THREAD_STREAM`; `LogJob = NaxLogJob | ThreadLogJob`; `ThreadLogJob { jobId; leaseEpoch; threadPath; lifecycle }`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-2: When `LogShipper` registers a `ThreadLogJob`, then it makes no PUT for `stdout`, `stderr` or `run`.

AC-3: When `drain('j1', 1, 5000)` runs on a registered `ThreadLogJob` whose file was appended after registration, then it resolves `'drained'` with the fake log server holding the whole file for `j1:1:thread`.
AC-4: When `drain('j1', 1, 5000)` runs on a registered `ThreadLogJob`, then the last PUT for stream `thread` has `final: true`.
AC-5: When `ServerClient.putLog` receives `stream: 'thread'`, then it requests a URL whose path is `/fleet/runner/jobs/j1/logs/thread`.

AC-6: When `NaxCapabilityProbe.probe` runs with a nax home whose `config.json` has `models.native` `{ balanced: 'minimax/MiniMax-M3' }` and fake `auth list` reports `minimax` available, then `threadBackends` equals `{ native: ['minimax/MiniMax-M3'], acp: [] }`.

AC-7: When `NaxCapabilityProbe.probe` runs with a nax home whose `config.json` has `models.native` `{ balanced: 'minimax/MiniMax-M3' }` and fake `auth list` reports `minimax` unavailable, then `threadBackends` equals `{ native: [], acp: [] }`.

AC-8: When `NaxCapabilityProbe.probe` runs with a nax home whose `config.json` has `models.native` `{ balanced: 'minimax/MiniMax-M3' }` and no profiles, then nax is called with arguments `['auth', 'list', '--json', 'minimax']`.
AC-9: When `NaxCapabilityProbe.probe` runs with a nax home without `config.json`, then `threadBackends` equals `{ native: [], acp: [] }`.
When an existing `NaxLogJob` with `sources.stdoutPath` containing `hello` is registered and drained, then the fake log server still holds `hello` for its `stdout` stream, preserving nax log shipping.

routing.reasoning: Log shipper union/nax auth-provider integration crosses modules; probing credential availability for session placement is security-sensitive and requires isolated tests.

modifiedFiles.reason: the exact `capabilities` object at line 76 gains `threadBackends: { native: [], acp: [] }`, because this story makes the nax probe always report thread backends; every other field stays as asserted.

userStories.title: ThreadJobRun start and preparation
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Once `ThreadJobRun` reaches RUNNING with a first turn ending `completed`, then the row's state events are exactly `[RUNNING]`.
AC-2: Once `ThreadJobRun` reaches RUNNING, then the shared recorder holds, in order, `credentials.acquire`, `prepareWorktree`, `credentials.release`, `ensureSkills`, `sessions.open`.
AC-3: When `prepareWorktree` is called during start, then its `feature` is `'brainstorm-x'`, `baseRef` equals ASSIGN's `ref`, and `credentialHelper` equals the acquired helper.
AC-4: When `ensureSkills` is called during start, then `skillsRoot` equals `<homeDir>/skills` and `skills` equals the fixture's skill sources.
AC-5: When `sessions.open` is called during start, then `worktree` equals the result of `prepareWorktree` and `approvalTimeoutSec` equals ASSIGN's timeout.
AC-6: When `start('prepare')` receives `{ ok: false, reason: 'worktree_conflict' }` from `prepareWorktree`, then state events are exactly `[FAILED]` with reason `worktree_conflict`.
AC-7: When `start('prepare')` receives `{ ok: false, reason: 'worktree_conflict' }` from `prepareWorktree`, then it calls `credentials.release`.
AC-8: When `start('prepare')` receives `{ ok: false, reason: 'worktree_conflict' }` from `prepareWorktree`, then it never calls `sessions.open`.
AC-9: When `start('prepare')` receives `{ ok: false, reason: 'worktree_conflict' }` from `prepareWorktree`, then it resolves with the row's `doneAt` set.
AC-10: When `start('prepare')` receives `{ ok: false, reason: 'skill_fetch_failed' }` from `ensureSkills`, then state events are exactly `[FAILED]` with reason `skill_fetch_failed`.
AC-11: When `start('prepare')` receives `{ ok: false, reason: 'model_unknown' }` from `sessions.open`, then state events are exactly `[FAILED]` with reason `model_unknown`.
AC-12: Once `ThreadJobRun` reaches RUNNING, then `logs.register` has `threadPath` equal to `<workspaceRoot>/.jobs/<jobId>/thread-events.jsonl`.
AC-13: Once `ThreadJobRun` reaches RUNNING, then the first line of `<jobDir>/thread-events.jsonl` has `type: 'session_started'` and `skillShas` equal to the fixture's skill source shas.
AC-14: Once `ThreadJobRun` reaches RUNNING, then the session's `send` is called with `'hi'`, the fixture's initial message text.
AC-15: Once `ThreadJobRun` reaches RUNNING, then the stream file's `input_consumed` line with `messageId: 'm1'` precedes the first session event line.

routing.reasoning: New long-lived session lifecycle with credential acquisition/release and async cancellation across steps is security-critical.

modifiedFiles.reason: the exact `TUNING` object gains `threadHeartbeatMs: 30_000` and `threadCloseTimeoutMs: 10_000`, because this story adds the thread heartbeat interval and the session close bound; it stays frozen.

userStories.title: ThreadJobRun turns, idle, caps and failure
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Drive turns and finish thread jobs on idle, cost, stream cap or session iteration failure with drain-before-transition ordering.

**Motivation** — Until a runner can run a `THREAD` job end to end, no thread can start.

**Approach** — **Turn.** Starting a turn sets the turn-running flag and stops the idle timer synchronously, then `writer.inputConsumed(messageId)` and every event of `session.send(text)` goes to `writer.event`. After each `usage` event, `spent >= Number(maxCostUsd)` closes with `cost_cap` (B3b-R4). After the iteration ends, `writer.flush()`, the flag clears and the idle timer restarts. A `turn_end` whose status is `errored`, `timed_out`, `cancelled` or `interrupted` leaves the session open. An iteration that throws (not during a close or after a halt) fails the run with `session_error`. Cost is counted from `usage.costUsd` only (`turn_end.costUsd` repeats the turn's usage), summed over the whole job, and compared as `spent >= Number(assign.maxCostUsd)`. The runner sends no `costSpentUsd` snapshot: the API's ingest (B2) adds usage to the job's spend.

**Idle.** The idle timer runs only while no turn runs; it expires after `threadIdleMs` and closes with `idle`.

**Close(reason)** — `reason` ∈ `idle`, `closed`, `cost_cap`, `stream_cap`, `cancelled`; the first one wins (B3b-R3); the closing flag is set and the turn-running check is made synchronously when the close is requested: stop the idle timer → if a turn runs, `session.cancel(reason)` and wait for its iteration to end → `session.close()` (a throw is logged) → `writer.flush()`, `writer.closed(reason)` → `logs.drain(jobId, leaseEpoch, logDrainTimeoutMs)` (a timeout is a `warn` lifecycle event) → stop the heartbeat → `UPLOADING` → `CANCELLED` `cancelled` when the reason is `cancelled`, else `COMPLETED` with the reason → `logs.stopJob`, `journal.markDone`.

**Fail(`session_error`)** — the same steps with `writer.failed('session_error')` in place of `writer.closed`, ending `UPLOADING → FAILED` `session_error`.

**Scope** — In: turn/idle/heartbeat/cap/failure and close internals on ThreadJobRun, fake session scripts and deterministic manual-clock tests. Out: command application and explicit cancellation (US-005), supervisor routing (US-006), API usage pricing (B2). The runner sends no `costSpentUsd` snapshot for a THREAD job (B3b-R4). Unpriced usage (`costSource` `unpriced`, `costUsd` 0) adds nothing to the spend; the API's budget rules govern it. A `maxCostUsd` of `'0'` closes the session with `cost_cap` at its first `usage` event (`0 >= 0`); the API's send rule `threads.costCap` refuses a send at that budget first.

**Interface** — `ThreadJobRun.start(from: RunStart): Promise<void>` persists until terminal + done; `ThreadEventWriter.event`, `flush`, `closed`, `failed`, `startHeartbeat`, `LogShipping.drain`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: When a turn ends `completed` and the manual clock advances by `threadIdleMs`, then state events are exactly `[RUNNING, UPLOADING, COMPLETED]` with COMPLETED reason `idle`.
AC-2: When idle close completes, then the last stream file line is `session_closed` with reason `'idle'`.
AC-3: When idle timer fires with `FakeLogShipping.holdDrain()`, then the row remains `RUNNING` until drain is released.
AC-4: When the clock advances by `threadIdleMs` while a held turn is still delivering events, then no `UPLOADING` event is recorded.
AC-5: When the manual clock advances by `threadHeartbeatMs` while the run is RUNNING, then the journal contains a `snapshot` event with a `heartbeatAt` string.
AC-6: When a turn ends `timed_out`, then the row remains `RUNNING`.
AC-7: When a turn ends `errored`, then the session's `close` has not been called.
AC-8: When a turn ends `interrupted`, then the row remains `RUNNING`.
AC-9: When `maxCostUsd` is `'1.00'` and turn `usage` events have `costUsd` 0.6 then 0.5, then session `cancel` is called.
AC-10: When `maxCostUsd` is `'1.00'` and turn `usage` events have `costUsd` 0.6 then 0.5, then job ends COMPLETED with reason `cost_cap`.
AC-11: When `maxCostUsd` is `'1.00'`, a turn has one `usage` event of `costUsd` 0.6, and `turn_end` also has `costUsd` 0.6, then the row remains `RUNNING`.
AC-12: When session turn throws after its first event, then state events are exactly `[RUNNING, UPLOADING, FAILED]` with FAILED reason `session_error`.
AC-13: When session turn throws after its first event, then the last stream line is `session_failed` with reason `'session_error'`.
AC-14: When tuning `streamMaxBytes` is 6000 and the first turn begins with a `thinking_delta` of 2000 characters, then the run ends COMPLETED with reason `stream_cap`.
AC-15: When start replaces an existing `<jobDir>/thread-events.jsonl` containing `{"type":"stale"}`, then the resulting stream file includes no `stale` line.

routing.reasoning: Concurrent session turns, cost accounting, close/drain race and shutdown semantics across an agent session require strict isolation.

userStories.title: ThreadJobRun commands and cancel
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply thread commands synchronously and add cancellation, halt and bounded abandon without blocking the fleet sync loop.

**Motivation** — An ABANDON with no run in memory waits on the repo mutex while `handleCommands` is awaited inline in the sync loop, stalling the whole loop behind a running RUN. A thread job needs its own run with its own stop paths.

**Approach** — B3-R5: a `THREAD_INPUT` while a turn runs is acked `rejected` with detail `turn_running`; the runner keeps no input queue. B3b-R2: a thread command is applied without awaiting a turn, a close or a drain. `CommandHandler.handle` is awaited inline by the sync loop, so `ThreadJobRun.command` is synchronous and every close runs in the background. B3b-R3: the first close reason wins. Once a run is closing or failing, a later idle expiry, cost cap, stream cap, `THREAD_CLOSE`, `CANCEL` or session error changes nothing.

**Commands** (`command(type, payload)`, all synchronous; a `THREAD_INPUT` that returns `ok` has already set the turn-running flag, so a second `THREAD_INPUT` in the same `CommandHandler.handle` batch gets `turn_running`):

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Run not yet `RUNNING` | `rejected` `session_not_ready` |
| Run closing or failing | `rejected` `session_closed` |
| `THREAD_INPUT` payload not `{ messageId: <segment>, text: <string of at most messageMaxBytes UTF-8 bytes> }` | `rejected` `invalid payload` |
| `THREAD_INPUT` while a turn runs | `rejected` `turn_running` (B3-R5) |
| `THREAD_INPUT` otherwise | `ok`; the turn starts in the background |
| `THREAD_ANSWER` payload not `{ requestId: <1..200 printable characters>, text: <string of at most messageMaxBytes UTF-8 bytes> }` | `rejected` `invalid payload` |
| `THREAD_ANSWER` | `session.answer(requestId, { text })`: `accepted` → `ok`; `expired`, `cancelled`, `unknown` → `rejected` with that word |
| `THREAD_STOP_TURN` | `ok`; `session.cancel('stopped')` when a turn runs, nothing otherwise; the session stays open |
| `THREAD_CLOSE` | `ok`; close `closed` in the background |
| `THREAD_PUBLISH` | `rejected` `unsupported` (phase C) |

**Cancel, halt, abandon.** `requestCancel()` before `RUNNING` records `cancelRequestedAt` (the next start step ends `CANCELLED`); while `RUNNING` it closes with `cancelled`; while closing it does nothing; it returns false only for a terminal row. `halt()` (daemon stop) sets the halted flag, calls `session.cancel('halted')` when a turn runs, stops the idle timer and the heartbeat, calls `logs.stopJob`, closes the session without awaiting it, and lets `start` resolve without waiting for the turn. After a halt, every background task of the run (the turn's iteration and tail, the idle timer, a close in progress, the heartbeat) writes no journal event, no stream line and no transition. `abandon()` halts, then `journal.abandon(jobId, leaseEpoch)` (which deletes the row and its events), then `credentials.release(row)` (a throw is logged), then awaits the close promise `halt()` started — `session.close()` is called once per run — for at most `threadCloseTimeoutMs` (a timeout or throw is logged). With `open` still pending there is no close to await: the session `open` resolves is closed then, unawaited. No mutex (B3b-R1), never longer than the close bound. The idle timer, the heartbeat and the close bound all wait through `deps.sleep` with an abort signal, so a manual clock drives them.

**Scope** — In: command (including `THREAD_PUBLISH` rejection), requestCancel, halt and abandon on ThreadJobRun; corresponding scripted-session tests. Out: CommandHandler/Supervisor routing (US-006), implementing phase C publish and phase D ACP. `THREAD_PUBLISH`, `write_doc`, a `PUBLISH` action, a stale session start and Discard belong to phase C; the runner rejects `PUBLISH` at ASSIGN and `THREAD_PUBLISH` as `unsupported`.

**Interface** — `command(type: ThreadCommandType, payload: unknown): ThreadCommandOutcome; requestCancel(): boolean; halt(): void; abandon(): Promise<void>;`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: When `command('THREAD_INPUT', { messageId: 'm2', text: 'next' })` is called, then session `send` receives `'next'`.
AC-2: When two `command('THREAD_INPUT', ...)` calls are made back to back with no await between them, then they return `{ result: 'ok' }` followed by `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'turn_running' }`.
AC-3: When `command('THREAD_INPUT', { messageId: '../m', text: 'x' })` is called, then it returns `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'invalid payload' }`.
AC-4: When `command('THREAD_INPUT', ...)` starts a held turn, then it returns `{ result: 'ok' }` while the turn is still delivering events.
AC-5: When `command('THREAD_ANSWER', { requestId: 'q1', text: 'yes' })` is called, then session `answer` receives `'q1'` and `{ text: 'yes' }`.
AC-6: When `command('THREAD_ANSWER', { requestId: 'q1', text: 'yes' })` has session `answer` return `'accepted'`, then it returns `{ result: 'ok' }`.
AC-7: When `command('THREAD_ANSWER', { requestId: 'q1', text: 'yes' })` has session `answer` return `'expired'`, then it returns `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'expired' }`.
AC-8: When `command('THREAD_STOP_TURN', {})` is called during a held turn, then session `cancel` is called.
AC-9: When `command('THREAD_STOP_TURN', {})` is called during a held turn, then the row remains `RUNNING` after that turn ends.
AC-10: When `command('THREAD_CLOSE', {})` is called, then job ends COMPLETED with reason `closed`.
AC-11: When `command('THREAD_CLOSE', {})` is called during a held turn, then the recorder places session `cancel` before session `close`.
AC-12: When `command('THREAD_INPUT', { messageId: 'm2', text: 'next' })` is called while the idle close's drain is held, then it returns `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'session_closed' }`.
AC-13: When `requestCancel()` is called while the idle close's drain is held and drain is then released, then job ends COMPLETED with reason `idle`.
AC-14: When `requestCancel()` is called while `sessions.open` is held and the open is then released, then state events are exactly `[CANCELLED]` with reason `cancelled before start`.
AC-15: When `requestCancel()` is called while `sessions.open` is held and the open is then released, then `close` is called on the session that `open` resolved.

routing.reasoning: Security-sensitive session commands plus racing halt, close, cancel, held iterations and bounded abandon.

userStories.title: Supervisor and CommandHandler for THREAD jobs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route THREAD ASSIGN, commands, READOPT and ABANDON via ThreadJobRun without reaping or blocking a concurrent RUN.

**Motivation** — Reusing the RUN path for thread rows would be unsafe: `Supervisor.reject` reaps the shared clone's `.nax-pids` since the job's creation (killing a concurrent RUN's nax), and an ABANDON with no run in memory waits on the repo mutex while `handleCommands` is awaited inline in the sync loop, stalling the whole loop behind a running RUN.

**Approach** — `SupervisorDeps` gains `threads?: ThreadRunSetup`. For a row whose `command` is `THREAD`:

- `begin(row, from)` creates a `ThreadJobRun` in the same run map; with no `threads` it transitions the row `FAILED` `backend_unavailable` and marks it done.
- `cancel` calls the run's `requestCancel` (the existing journal path when no run is in memory).
- `abandon` with a run awaits `run.abandon()` (bounded by `threadCloseTimeoutMs`); with no run it calls `journal.abandon` and then `threads.host.credentials.release(row)` (a throw is logged) — never a `JobRun`, never the mutex.
- The run map entry and `pending` promise are the `start()` promise, as for `JobRun`, so `idle()` waits for thread runs too; a halted thread run resolves without waiting for its turn.
- `readopt`: terminal → `markDone`, `ok`, no executor call; `ASSIGNED` with `pid` null → `begin(row, 'reprepare')`, `ok`; any other state → `markDone`, `rejected` `thread session ended by a runner restart`, with no `killIfOurs`, `executor.reap` or `executor.cleanup`.
- `threadCommand(command: FleetCommandOut): ThreadCommandOutcome` — the run for `(jobId, leaseEpoch)` when it is a `ThreadJobRun`, else `rejected` `does not hold job`.

`CommandHandler.apply` routes `THREAD_INPUT`, `THREAD_ANSWER`, `THREAD_STOP_TURN`, `THREAD_CLOSE` and `THREAD_PUBLISH` to `supervisor.threadCommand` and records the outcome with `record` (a re-sent command id is acked from the record, never re-applied).

**Scope** — In: Supervisor routing, lifecycle and CommandHandler acknowledgement/dedupe, using FakeExecutor to pin absence of cleanup. Out: daemon wiring and protocol version (US-007); no thread uses JobExecutor.reap, killIfOurs or cleanup.

**Interface** — `SupervisorDeps.threads?: ThreadRunSetup; Supervisor.threadCommand(command: FleetCommandOut): ThreadCommandOutcome`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: When `CommandHandler.handle([<THREAD ASSIGN>])` runs, then the THREAD row reaches `RUNNING`.
AC-2: When `CommandHandler.handle([<THREAD ASSIGN>])` runs on a Supervisor without `threads`, then the row ends `FAILED` with reason `backend_unavailable`.
AC-3: When `CommandHandler.handle([<THREAD_INPUT for a RUNNING thread job>])` runs, then it acks `{ result: 'ok' }`.
AC-4: When `CommandHandler.handle([<THREAD_INPUT>])` is sent twice with the same command id, then session `send` receives its text once in total.
AC-5: When `CommandHandler.handle([<THREAD_INPUT for a job id the runner never assigned>])` runs, then it acks `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'does not hold job' }`.

AC-6: When `CommandHandler.handle([<THREAD_CLOSE>])` completes, `Supervisor.idle()` resolves, and then `handle([<THREAD_INPUT>])` runs for that job, then the input is acked `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'does not hold job' }`.
AC-7: When `CommandHandler.handle([<CANCEL for a RUNNING thread job>])` runs, then the row's state events end in `[UPLOADING, CANCELLED]`.
AC-8: Given a RUN job of the same repo holds the repo mutex with a held FakeExecutor watch, when `handle([<ABANDON for a RUNNING thread job>])` runs, then it resolves while RUN still holds the mutex.
AC-9: When `handle([<ABANDON for a RUNNING thread job>])` finishes, then `journal.getJob(jobId, leaseEpoch)` is `null`.
AC-10: When `handle([<ABANDON for a RUNNING thread job>])` encounters a session whose `close` never resolves, then it resolves once the manual clock passes `threadCloseTimeoutMs`.
AC-11: When `handle([<ABANDON for a RUNNING thread job>])` runs, then `credentials.release` is called for that row.
AC-12: When `handle([<ABANDON for a RUNNING thread job>])` runs during a held turn and the turn is subsequently released, then `journal.pendingEvents(jobId, leaseEpoch, 100)` is empty.
AC-13: Given a RUN of the same repo holds the repo mutex, when `handle([<ABANDON for a RUNNING thread row with no run in memory>])` runs, then it resolves while RUN still holds the mutex.
AC-14: When `handle([<READOPT for a RUNNING thread row with no run in memory>])` runs, then it acks `{ result: 'rejected', detail: 'thread session ended by a runner restart' }`.
AC-15: When `handle([<READOPT for a RUNNING thread row with no run in memory>])` runs, then FakeExecutor receives no `reap`, `cleanup` or `kill` call.

userStories.title: Daemon wiring and protocol 4
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire thread sessions and reporting into the fleet daemon, prune thread assets and advertise protocol v4.

**Motivation** — B1 places `THREAD` jobs only on runners that report protocol 4, and B3a built the session host's parts without wiring them. Until a runner can run a `THREAD` job end to end, no thread can start.

**Approach** — `DaemonOptions` gains `threadSessions?: Pick<ThreadSessionFactory, 'open'>` and `configureCredentials?: (config: CredentialsConfig) => void` (default nax-agent's). `startDaemon` calls `configureCredentials(naxCredentialsConfig(config.naxHome))` once, before the first sync.

`threadNativeModels(naxHome, latest: () => RunnerCapabilities | null): () => Promise<NativeModelSet>` (`thread/thread-host.ts`) reads the native models for the providers whose credential `available` is true in `latest()` (none when `latest()` is null). `latest()` is the bounded report of the last probe (start, every `capabilityProbeMs`, SIGHUP), so a provider logged in since then is seen at the next probe. The default session factory is `new ThreadSessionFactory({ homeDir: home.dir, naxHome: config.naxHome, nativeModels: threadNativeModels(config.naxHome, () => reporter.latest()) })`.

The Supervisor gets `threads: { host: { sessions, credentials: broker, git, homeDir: home.dir, workspaceRoot }, tuning }` in nax mode; with a runner.json `capabilities` override it receives no thread host (the override does not report threadBackends and cannot host threads).

`freeSlots` = `freeSlots(capacity, journal.activeCountExcluding('THREAD'))`; the server counts thread slots (B1-R1).

The sync loop's `onArchivedThreads` keeps the latest `archivedThreadIds` (an absent field keeps the previous list). The job prune (start and every `pruneIntervalMs`) also runs `pruneArchivedThreads({ git, homeDir: home.dir, threadIds: <latest list>, activeThreadIds: <thread.threadId of every active THREAD row> })` and `pruneSkillCache(<home.dir>/skills, now())`; a throw is a `warn` log.

`FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` becomes 4 (sync and enroll both send it).

**Integration setup** — Each `[integration]` criterion runs `startDaemon` in nax mode (a runner config with no `capabilities` block and a `FakeNaxCli` that answers the version, trust, profile, sandbox and `auth list` calls, as `test/unit/daemon.spec.ts` does from line 365) against the fake fleet server defined in `test/unit/daemon-thread.spec.ts` (Creates), with injected `threadSessions` (the fake factory from `test/helpers/fake-agent-session.ts`) and `configureCredentials`, a `file://` clone, `selfCommand: [process.execPath, <src/main.ts>]`, tuning `pruneIntervalMs: 50`, and THREAD ASSIGN fixtures with `skills: []` (no skill fetch leaves the machine). The fake fleet server needs a `thread` log route and an `archivedThreadIds` knob.

**Scope** — In: daemon start/probe/credentials/supervisor, sync archived callback, journal count, prune, shared protocol version for sync and enroll and corresponding unit/integration tests. Out: B2 API stream ingest/pricing, phase C publish and edits to generated agent guidance. A runner configured with a runner.json `capabilities` block reports no `threadBackends` and hosts no threads.

**Interface** — `threadNativeModels(naxHome: string, latest: () => RunnerCapabilities | null): () => Promise<NativeModelSet>`; `DaemonOptions.threadSessions?: Pick<ThreadSessionFactory, 'open'>; DaemonOptions.configureCredentials?: (config: CredentialsConfig) => void`; `SyncLoopDeps.onArchivedThreads?: (ids) => void`; `Journal.activeCountExcluding(command)`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: When `startDaemon` starts in nax mode, then injected `configureCredentials` is called exactly once with a config whose `configDir()` returns `config.naxHome`.

AC-2: When nax home's `config.json` has `models.native` `{ balanced: 'minimax/MiniMax-M3' }` and `minimax` is available, then the daemon's first sync has `capabilities.threadBackends` equal to `{ native: ['minimax/MiniMax-M3'], acp: [] }`.
AC-3: When fake fleet server delivers a THREAD ASSIGN, then it receives a `thread` log PUT for that job whose first line has `type: 'session_started'`.
AC-4: Given capacity 2 and one RUNNING THREAD job, when the daemon syncs next, then it reports `freeSlots` 2.
AC-5: Given one active RUN row and one active THREAD row, when `Journal.activeCountExcluding('THREAD')` runs, then it returns 1.
AC-6: When `SyncLoop` receives a response with `archivedThreadIds: ['t1']`, then it calls `onArchivedThreads` with `['t1']`.
AC-7: When a sync responds with `archivedThreadIds: ['t9']` and the next prune pass runs, then `<home>/threads/t9` no longer exists.
AC-8: When a sync responds with `archivedThreadIds: ['t1']` while thread `t1`'s job is RUNNING and the next prune pass runs, then `<home>/threads/t1` remains.
AC-9: When a `<home>/skills/<sourceId>/<sha>` directory has mtime 31 days ago and the next prune pass runs, then the directory is gone.

AC-10: When `threadNativeModels(naxHome, () => caps)` reads `caps.credentials` with `minimax` available and `zai` unavailable over tiers `{ fast: 'minimax/MiniMax-M2.7', balanced: 'zai/glm-5' }`, then it resolves `models: ['minimax/MiniMax-M2.7']`.
AC-11: When `threadNativeModels(naxHome, () => null)` runs, then it resolves `{ models: [], defaultModel: null }`.
AC-12: When the daemon sends its first sync, then `protocolVersion` is 4.

analysis: Graph-first codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this session, so navigation fell back to targeted direct reads of spec-named files; line citations below refer to current worktree. Existing Bun/TypeScript runner is the sole session host; apps/api is the system of record, and @nathapp/fleet-protocol is the shared wire contract. B3a is already present: native tier discovery/readNativeModels and provider extraction (apps/runner/src/thread/native-models.ts:10-52), the read-only native session factory with ACP refused, model allowlist, carryHistoryAcrossModels, resume and persistent transcript (apps/runner/src/thread/session-factory.ts:70-145), redacting/capped thread event writer with held deltas and paced shipper wake (apps/runner/src/thread/thread-event-writer.ts:70-80,158-213,337-408), credential config (apps/runner/src/thread/nax-credentials.ts:18-32), worktree preparation and pruning (apps/runner/src/thread/thread-worktree.ts:22-43), and safe skill cache (apps/runner/src/thread/skill-fetch.ts:9-49). Contract types, command names and limits already exist (packages/fleet-protocol/src/threads.ts:1-58); capabilities already permit optional threadBackends while FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 3 (packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts:1-8,65-75). US-001: parseAssign currently rejects THREAD, validates base fields then copies a whitelisted AssignPayload (apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:34-82); add strict THREAD-specific validation at the appropriate point, and reject a thread key on all other kinds; paths must use assertSegment/assertFeature, byte-length not character count for initialMessage. US-002: LogJob currently requires nax sources and LogStreamName only includes old events (apps/runner/src/logs/types.ts:1-60); LogShipper.register and lacksRun/discover unconditionally dereference sources (apps/runner/src/logs/log-shipper.ts:76-91,140-149,180-199); narrow discriminated union for thread-only registration while preserving upload/offset/refusal/drain behavior. NaxCapabilityProbe auth list currently uses profile providers only and bounds full capability report (apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.ts:118-158,166-188,222-240); union native tier providers for the auth call, filter available credentials for threadBackends, keep 64 KiB bound. StaticCapabilityProbe just clones config (apps/runner/src/capabilities/capability-probe.ts:24-32) and must not advertise threads. US-003–005: implement ThreadJobRun independently of JobRun, with a long-lived start promise, synchronous commands, guarded asynchronous turns/close, first-close-wins, cancellable sleep timers, no shared repo mutex except inside prepareThreadWorktree and no executor reaping. JobRunDeps/RunStart are defined in apps/runner/src/supervisor/job-run.ts:33-69; its normal run holds a repo mutex (line 105-123), so do not reuse it. JobEvents enforces legal transition sequences and bounds payloads (apps/runner/src/supervisor/job-events.ts:17-52), heartbeat helper uses abortable sleep (apps/runner/src/supervisor/heartbeat.ts:1-17), real journal stores ASSIGN JSON and contiguous event seq (apps/runner/src/journal/journal.ts:119-194), and credential broker returns a helper and releases epoch sockets (apps/runner/src/credentials/broker.ts:11-32,73-100). Preserve no post-halt journal/stream writes even if held turn/open resolves later, close a late-opened session, bound abandon close and free credentials; new stream file must be reset per epoch. Tuning currently has thread idle/wake/search/skill timeouts but not heartbeat/close (apps/runner/src/daemon/tuning.ts:1-77). US-006: Supervisor maps only JobRun and readopt rejection kills/reaps/cleans (apps/runner/src/supervisor/supervisor.ts:20-42,58-122), which is dangerous for THREAD; route all THREAD branches before executor/repo-mutex paths, including no-in-memory abandon/readopt and bounded close. CommandHandler.apply currently falls through for thread commands and persists acks by command id (apps/runner/src/supervisor/command-handler.ts:23-98); route synchronously to supervisor and record once. US-007: daemon currently probes, initializes broker/shipper/supervisor, computes freeSlots from all active rows, and runs only job prune (apps/runner/src/daemon/daemon.ts:101-206); introduce credential configuration and session factory before first sync, thread-aware active count, archived-thread callback/prune and skill-cache prune, preserving crash/stop behavior (line 209-237). SyncLoop.apply processes response and awaits handleCommands inline (apps/runner/src/sync/sync-loop.ts:132-161), making synchronous thread-command application and non-mutex ABANDON vital. CapabilityReporter.latest is bounded probe result (apps/runner/src/capabilities/capability-probe.ts:54-86). Tests use bun:test, real :memory: SQLite and files; existing fake shipping/clock support deterministic drain and abort (apps/runner/test/helpers/fake-log-shipping.ts:1-62, apps/runner/test/helpers/manual-clock.ts:1-31). Existing RUN/PLAN parser regression assertions already live in apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.spec.ts:9-21; existing probe's exact capability-object test (apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.spec.ts), tuning frozen-object test (apps/runner/src/daemon/tuning.spec.ts), sync version assertion (apps/runner/src/sync/batch.spec.ts), and daemon version assertion (apps/runner/test/unit/daemon.spec.ts) need updates to their changed fields/expected 4, without losing other fields. Enrollment also reads the same protocol constant (apps/runner/src/commands/enroll.ts:123) while sync request builds it in apps/runner/src/sync/batch.ts:68. New test double should record ordered operations, holds, cancel and close; daemon integration uses fake fleet server, FakeNaxCli, real file:// git. Dependency order: 001 and 002 independently, 003 -> 004 -> 005 -> 006, then 007; 007 also changes fleet-protocol. Backward compatibility: preserve RUN/PLAN/config parse, log sources, normal JobRun readopt and sync acks, bounded capability reports and static-override no-host behavior; v4 is an incompatible fleet handshake and B2 thread ingest is not shipped, so leave FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED off. Build gates: bun run type-check and bun run lint in apps/runner for each story, plus root bun run type-check for 007; do not modify generated clients or AGENTS/context files.
outOfScope: The API accepting, folding and pricing the `thread` stream, cost accounting from `usage` lines and the content SSE belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-ingest` (B2); until then the API refuses `PUT .../logs/thread` and `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` stays off.
The runner sends no `costSpentUsd` snapshot for a THREAD job (B3b-R4).
`THREAD_PUBLISH`, `write_doc`, a `PUBLISH` action, a stale session start and Discard belong to phase C; the runner rejects `PUBLISH` at ASSIGN and `THREAD_PUBLISH` as `unsupported`.
ACP session backends belong to phase D; `threadBackends.acp` is always `[]`.
A runner configured with a runner.json `capabilities` block reports no `threadBackends` and hosts no threads.
A daemon stop or crash ends a live session without a `session_closed` line; READOPT then rejects the job, the API marks it CRASHED, and the next message starts a new job with `resume: true`.
Replaying a turn interrupted by a restart is not done; nax-agent reports it `interrupted` and the next input is a new turn.
Unpriced usage (`costSource` `unpriced`, `costUsd` 0) adds nothing to the spend; the API's budget rules govern it.
A `maxCostUsd` of `'0'` closes the session with `cost_cap` at its first `usage` event (`0 >= 0`); the API's send rule `threads.costCap` refuses a send at that budget first.

Unpriced usage (`costSource` `unpriced`, `costUsd` 0) adds nothing to the spend; the API's budget rules govern it. A `maxCostUsd` of `'0'` closes the session with `cost_cap` at its first `usage` event (`0 >= 0`); the API's send rule `threads.costCap` refuses a send at that budget first.

A thread whose spend has overshot its cap gives a negative remaining `maxCostUsd`, which `COST_RE` rejects at ASSIGN (`invalid maxCostUsd`); the API's send rule `threads.costCap` refuses before that. A clamp in the API is a B1 follow-up.
The runner `context.md` (`.nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md`, "protocol v3") is updated by hand after merge.

B3a's waived review items (`ensureClone`'s optional identity, base-ref resolution duplicating `resolveRef`, the event writer taking plain strings for reasons, the skill fetcher's unused `filePath` alias and single-`dir` branch) are not changed.
US-001 only: `instructions` length, `resume` type, `skills` element shapes, a backend `effort` and an `acp` backend's `agent` value share the field table without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-002 only: `wake`, `stopJob` and the shipper's refusal handling for a `thread` stream share the existing stream rules without a dedicated acceptance criterion; so does `StaticCapabilityProbe` reporting no `threadBackends` (unchanged code).

US-003 only: a cancel or halt between the start steps, a credentials refusal, a throwing start step, a start with no initial message and `'watch'` / `'finish'` starts share the step rules without a dedicated acceptance criterion; so does `onWarn`.
US-004 only: the drain timeout warning, the heartbeat stopping at `UPLOADING` and `session.close()` being called by the idle close share the close steps without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-005 only: `session_not_ready`, `THREAD_ANSWER` payload validation, the `cancelled` and `unknown` answer statuses `THREAD_PUBLISH` (`unsupported`) and `requestCancel()` while `RUNNING` (pinned through `CANCEL` in US-006) share the command table without a dedicated acceptance criterion; so does `halt()` (pinned through ABANDON in US-006).

US-006 only: a terminal or `ASSIGNED` thread row at READOPT, `cancel` with no run in memory, a thread command for a RUN job, and a throwing `session.close()` or `credentials.release` in `abandon()` share the existing Supervisor paths without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
US-007 only: a prune that throws and an absent `archivedThreadIds` share the prune rules without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
